claims.text: There are 36 agent files in .claude/agents/.
All 36 agent files conform to a shared frontmatter convention with fields: name, description, tools, model, effort, skills, memory.
No agent currently has any mcp__<server>__<tool> entry in its tools allowlist (verified by grep -rn 'mcp__' .claude/agents/ returning zero hits).
The seven-server feature introduces the mcp__ pattern to agent tools allowlists for the first time in this repo.
GitNexus is the likely-consumer mapping target for discovery-codebase-researcher (PRIMARY per ADR-0007 v2.2.0) and review-architecture-auditor (also names it as primary).
codebase-memory-mcp is the likely-consumer mapping target for discovery-codebase-researcher (FALLBACK) and review-architecture-auditor (FALLBACK).
Serena is the likely consumer for discovery-codebase-researcher (symbol-level value contingent on UI-8 narrowing — repo is markdown-heavy).
mcp-openapi-schema is the likely consumer for design-api.
actionlint-mcp is the likely consumer for design-cicd.
HashiCorp Terraform MCP is the likely consumer for design-iac.
Context7 is the likely consumer for discovery-external-researcher and is also a documentation-lookup fallback referenced from KB-cc-platform/SKILL.md:109.
Exa is the likely consumer for discovery-external-researcher.

The Claude Code trifecta consists of KB-cc-platform (7 refs + 9 templates), KB-cc-design (2 refs), and auditing-cc-configs (FAMILY COORDINATOR; 6 refs + 6+ scripts) and is complete; its audit half name has a trailing '-configs' deviation.

The Codespaces trifecta consists of KB-codespaces-platform (10 refs + 5 templates including subdirs), KB-codespaces-design (2 refs), and auditing-codespaces, and its audit half is a STUB per ADR-0033.

The GitHub Actions trifecta consists of KB-github-actions-platform (19 refs + 21 templates), KB-github-actions-design (2 refs), and auditing-github-actions (1 ref + 1 script; uses auditing-shared per ADR-0031), and is complete.

The MCP trifecta (this feature) consists of KB-mcp-platform (NEW), KB-mcp-design (NEW), and auditing-mcp (4 refs + 4 scripts + 2 examples; augmented per FR-11-c); the audit half exists while the platform and design halves are greenfield.

The primary/fallback wiring is a four-layer prose chain: ADR-0007 (canonical) -> ADR-0018 (cross-ref) -> KB-codebase-research (consumer skill) -> discovery-codebase-researcher (consumer agent), with no structured field anywhere.
The auditing-mcp skill explicitly declares membership in the auditing-cc-configs family at SKILL.md line 30.
auditing-github-actions consumes auditing-shared per ADR-0031 (canonical helper home).
Both code-graph MCPs (GitNexus and codebase-memory-mcp) are referenced in seven existing corpus files but registered in zero (.mcp.json is absent).
The .mcp.json blast radius is universally shallow but universally broad — every Claude Code session reads it, and a typo breaks every session.
Adding GitNexus tools to discovery-codebase-researcher.md tools allowlist is a convention-introduction event: it is the first agent to carry mcp__ entries, and the chosen pattern becomes de facto.

The devcontainer Dockerfile + devcontainer.json surface is historically fragile (twice-fixed recently), and a seven-server install adds substantial layer count plus toolchain constraints (no Go, no DinD for GitNexus + Terraform MCP).
The auditing-mcp augmentation stretches scope from 'config audit' to also 'runtime audit'.
Agent file frontmatter requires name and description; tools, model, effort, skills, and memory are common fields.
The tools: field syntax is mixed — both bracketed array form (tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, ...]) and comma form (tools: Read, Grep, Glob, ...) appear in agent files.
Bash restriction patterns use both Bash(name:*) and Bash(name *) forms.
The MCP tool naming convention is mcp__<server>__<tool> for specific tools and mcp__<server> for whole-server permission grants, documented in KB-cc-platform but not yet used in any agent file.

Per ADR-0020, skill directories are named KB-<topic>-platform/, KB-<topic>-design/, and auditing-<topic>/, with frontmatter name field lowercase-hyphenated, with one naming deviation: auditing-cc-configs (trailing '-configs').

A primary/fallback expression convention does NOT exist as a structured convention today; the current expression is pure prose, four layers (ADR-0007 -> ADR-0018 -> KB-codebase-research -> discovery-codebase-researcher).
The only lifecycle hook in use in devcontainer.json today is onCreateCommand, executing 'claude --version && python3 --version && node --version && gh --version'.

Feature pin policy in devcontainer.json is mixed and inconsistent: common-utils:2 major-pinned; github-cli:1 with version 'latest'; node:1 with version 'lts'; claude-code:1 major-pinned. No exact-version pin is in use.
containerEnv currently holds only EDITOR and PAGER (non-secret) — empty of credentials, confirming NFR-2-a baseline.
The devcontainer image base is mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:1-${PYTHON_VERSION}-bookworm with PYTHON_VERSION=3.11.
Commit 5e7f4ac fixed a base-image stale-Yarn-key devcontainer build failure; the surface has demonstrated breakability.
Design halves of the trifectas carry exactly two references files named patterns-and-anti-patterns.md and principles.md — a STRONG convention.
Design halves carry no assets/templates/ — a STRONG convention.
Platform halves have many references files (KB-cc=7, KB-codespaces=10, KB-gha=19) and assets/templates/ subdirectories (KB-cc=9 .example, KB-codespaces=5, KB-gha=21).
Platform halves carry no scripts/ subdirectory today per ADR-0031 relocation; audit half carries Python audit scripts.
Cross-reference style: platform-half description ends with 'Pairs with KB-<sister>-design' and design-half description ends with 'Pairs with KB-<sister>-platform'.
Audit-half family membership is declared via a body line (e.g., 'This skill is part of the auditing-cc-configs family'), not in frontmatter.

There is no log-rotation, log-tail, or log-path convention in the repo to reuse — FR-10 / UI-12 starts greenfield.
